dervis-irab:1-14.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الشَّفْعِ) The pair of number. One says: "ashafʿ is it or witr?", i.e. even or odd; its plural is ashfāʿ and shifāʿ. The maṣdar of shafaʿa, yashfaʿu (of the pattern fataḥa) is shafʿ, i.e. he made the thing shafʿ, a pair, by adding its like to it; one says: "it was odd and he paired it (shafaʿahu) with another", i.e. joined it to it. In the Qāmūs: "al-shafʿ is the opposite of al-witr, namely the pair; shafaʿahu, like manaʿahu; and the Day of Aḍḥā. It is said regarding His saying, the Exalted, «والشفع والوتر» that it is creation, because of His saying, the Exalted, «ومن كل شيء خلقنا زوجين», or that it is Allah, mighty and majestic, because of His saying, the Exalted, «ما يكون من نجوى ثلاثة إلا هو رابعهم»."
(الْوَتْرِ) In the Qāmūs: "al-witr, with kasra or with fatḥa, is the single, or what has not been paired of number; and the Day of ʿArafa."
Abū Ḥayyān said: "'al-Shafʿ and al-witr': it is mentioned in the book al-Taḥrīr wa-l-Taḥbīr that there are thirty-six views about them, which we grew weary of reading, let alone of writing in this book of ours."
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "They have said a great deal about the shafʿ and the witr, until they almost exhausted most of what they could fall upon, and that is of very little profit, and deserves to be disregarded."
(حِجْرٍ) Intellect. The intellect is so called because it restrains (yaḥjuru) its owner from what is not lawful or fitting, just as it is called ʿaql because it restrains (yaʿqilu) its owner from vile things and forbids him, and because it forbids what is not lawful or fitting. The root meaning of ḥijr is prevention; this root has been discussed before. Ibn Khālawayh said: "هل في ذلك حجر means: for one who has intellect and understanding." Al-Ḥijr is also the dwellings of Thamūd, the Ḥijr of the Kaʿba, and the female horse.
(جابُوا) They cut through. In al-Mukhtār: "jāba: he pierced and cut through, and its pattern is qāla; of it is His saying, the Exalted, «وثمود الذين جابوا الصخر بالواد»; and 'I cut through the lands' (jubtu), with ḍamma on the jīm, of the pattern qāla and bāʿa; and ajabtuhā: I cut through them."

* I'rab:
(وَالْفَجْرِ وَلَيالٍ عَشْرٍ) The واو is a particle of oath and genitive; الفجر is genitive by the oath-wāw, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to "I swear"; the واو is a conjunction; and ليال is conjoined to الفجر, genitive, its genitive sign being the fatḥa as a substitute for the kasra implied on the omitted yāʾ, because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. Ibn Mālik pointed to this important rule in his saying:
وكن لجمع مشبه مفاعلا ... أو المفاعيل بمنع كافلا
(And be, for a plural resembling mafāʿil or al-mafāʿīl, a guarantor of the prohibition [of tanwīn].)
That is, a plural resembling mafāʿil or al-mafāʿīl, in having a fatḥa on the first letter and an alif as the third, followed by two letters like mafāʿil, or three letters whose middle is quiescent like mafāʿīl, is barred from ṣarf because the plural in it stands in place of two causes, namely plurality and the absence of a parallel in the singular. His saying "mafāʿil" includes what begins with a mīm, like masājid, or with another letter, like darāhim; and his saying "al-mafāʿīl" includes what begins with a mīm, like maṣābīḥ, or with another letter, like danānīr. Then, of this plural there is one that comes with a weak final radical, in two kinds. One is that in which the kasra after the alif is turned into fatḥa, so the yāʾ turns into alif, like ʿadhārā, and there is no difficulty in the prohibition of tanwīn. The other is that in which the fatḥa is found heavy in its class and is dropped, and the tanwīn attaches to it; to that he pointed in his saying:
وذا اعتلال منه كالجواري ... رفعا وجرّا أجره كساري
(And what is weak of it, like al-jawārī, in nominative and genitive treat like sārī.)
He means that what is of the plural with a weak final radical, like jawārin, being as described in the dropping of the vowel, is treated like sārin in having tanwīn attached to its end in the nominative and genitive; so you say "hādhihi jawārin" and "marartu bi-jawārin". He kept silent about the accusative, so it is understood that it follows the original rule, like the sound word; so you say "raʾaytu jawāriya".
And عشر is an adjective of ليال. They said that by the ten nights he meant the ten of Dhū l-Ḥijja, and it came indefinite because of their superiority over other nights of the year; it is also said that they are the last ten of Ramaḍān, and that they are the first ten of Muḥarram. (وَالشَّفْعِ وَالْوَتْرِ وَاللَّيْلِ إِذا يَسْرِ) Conjoined to الفجر and ليال, and likewise الوتر and الليل; and إذا is an adverbial attached to the omitted verb of the oath, or to an implied verb of oath, and Abū l-Baqāʾ went that way, i.e. "I swear by the night at the time of its journeying". يسري is an imperfect verb taken from al-sarā, which is particular to journeying by night, and it has been treated before. He said in al-Miṣbāḥ: "saraytu al-layl and saraytu bihi, sarā; the noun is al-sarāya, when you traverse it by traveling; and asraytu, with alif, is a Ḥijāzī dialect; both are used transitively with the bāʾ to an object, so one says 'saraytu bi-Zayd' and 'asraytu bihi'. Al-surya, with ḍamma or fatḥa on the sīn, is more specific; one says 'we journeyed a surya of the night'; the plural is al-surā, like mudya and mudā. Abū Zayd said: al-sarā may be at the beginning of the night, its middle and its end. The Arabs used sarā for abstract things, likening them to bodies, figuratively and by extension. Allah the Exalted said: «والليل إذا يسر», and the meaning is: when it passes. Al-Baghawī said: when it travels and goes. Al-Fārābī said: 'poison and wine and the like sarā in him'. Al-Saraqusṭī said: 'the vein of evil sarā in the human being', and Ibn al-Qaṭṭāʿ added to that: 'sarā ʿalayhi al-hamm' means it came to him at night, and 'sarā hammuhu' means it went. Ascribing the verb to abstractions is frequent in their speech, such as 'the phantom wandered', 'the worry went', 'sloth and vigor seized him'; and the saying of the jurists 'the wound sarā to the soul' means its pain continued until death resulted from it; and 'his palm was cut off and it sarā to his forearm', i.e. the effect of the wound extended; and 'the prohibition sarā' and 'the emancipation sarā', in the sense of extension. These words are current on the tongues of the jurists, and have no mention in the well-known books, but they are consistent with what preceded." Some of the readers dropped the yāʾ of يسر in pause and kept it in continuation; some kept it in both cases, and some dropped it in both cases because it is absent in the script of the noble codex and to conform to the verse-endings. The wording of Ibn Khālawayh: "The original was yasrī, but they cut short the yāʾ so that it resembles the verse-endings before it; so among the readers there are those who keep the yāʾ according to the original, and those who drop it, following the codex." (هَلْ فِي ذلِكَ قَسَمٌ لِذِي حِجْرٍ) The sense of the interrogative here is magnification and glorification of the things sworn by; في ذلك is a fronted predicate; قسم is a postponed mubtadaʾ; and لذي حجر is an adjective. On this view هل and what is within its scope are the response to the oath. It is also said that it is for affirmation, as in your saying "Have I not shown you favor?" when you did show favor. The response on this view is omitted, implied, its implied form being "We shall surely requite everyone according to what he did", and al-Zamakhsharī implied "you will surely be punished". It is also said that the response is mentioned, namely «إن ربك لبالمرصاد». The wording of al-Samīn: "Muqātil said: هل here is in the place of إن, its implied form being 'indeed in that is an oath for one of intellect', so هل on this view is in the position of the response to the oath. This is a false statement, because it is not fit to be what is sworn upon, even supposing the construction is so; I mention it only to draw attention to its invalidity." (أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِعادٍ، إِرَمَ ذاتِ الْعِمادِ الَّتِي لَمْ يُخْلَقْ مِثْلُها فِي الْبِلادِ) The hamza is for affirmative interrogation, i.e. "you have seen", because what is meant by seeing here is the seeing of the heart, which is knowledge; it was expressed by seeing because it is necessary knowledge equal in clarity and manifestness to witnessing and eyesight. لم is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive; تر is an imperfect verb jussive by لم; كيف is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative by a verb, as a maṣdar, and al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn Hishām in al-Mughnī preferred it; the meaning is: "what action did your Lord do". Ibn Khālawayh parsed it as ḥāl; he said: "كيف is a question about the state." But that is impermissible, because if it is parsed as ḥāl it would be from the agent, and describing Him, the Exalted, with modality is impossible and not allowed. The clause suspended by the interrogative كيف takes the place of the two objects of تر. فعل ربك is a past verb and an agent; وبعاد are two [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to فعل; and إرم is a badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) of عاد, and is barred from ṣarf for being a proper name and feminine. This substitution is a notification that they are the first, ancient ʿĀd. It is also said that Iram is their city or their land in which they were. The wording of Abū l-Baqāʾ: "Iram is not declined because of definiteness and femininity. It is said it is the name of a tribe; on that view the implied form is 'Iram, the owner of ذات العماد', because ذات العماد is a city. It is also said that ذات العماد is a description, as you say 'the tribe possessing kingship'. It is also said that Iram is a city; on that view the implied form is 'ʿĀd, the owner of Iram'. It is read بعاد إرم by annexation, requiring no implication, and it is read إرم ذات العماد with genitive by
annexation." ذات العماد is an adjective of إرم, i.e. of tallness. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "ذات العماد, if it is a description of the tribe, means that they were bedouins, people of tent-poles, or tall in body, likening their stature to pillars; of it is the saying 'a muʿmad man' and 'ʿummadān' when he is tall. It is also said: possessing lofty building. If it is a description of the city, the meaning is that it has columns." A summary of its wonderful story will come in the section of Benefits. التي is a second adjective of إرم; the clause لم يخلق is the ṣila of التي; مثلها is the deputy agent of يخلق; and في البلاد are two [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to يخلق. It was read يخلق in the active, in which case مثلها is a direct object. (وَثَمُودَ الَّذِينَ جابُوا الصَّخْرَ بِالْوادِ) The واو is a conjunction; ثمود is conjoined to عاد; الذين is an adjective of ثمود; the clause جابوا is the ṣila of الذين; الصخر is a direct object; and بالوادي are two [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to جابوا, the باء being locative, hence meaning "in"; the yāʾ was dropped because it is one of the supplementary yāʾs. (وَفِرْعَوْنَ ذِي الْأَوْتادِ) Conjoined to عاد; and ذي الأوتاد is an adjective of فرعون: he used to drive four stakes for the one he tortured, and bind him with them stretched on the ground, and then torture him as he wished, by beating, burning and other means. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "al-watid, with kasra on the tāʾ, in the dialect of the Ḥijāz, which is the most eloquent, and its plural is awtād; with fatḥa on the tāʾ is a dialect; the people of Najd put sukūn on the tāʾ and assimilate after the conversion, leaving wadd. watadtu al-watid, atidu, watdan (of the pattern waʿada): I fixed it in a wall or the ground; and awtadtuhu, with alif, is a dialect." (الَّذِينَ طَغَوْا فِي الْبِلادِ فَأَكْثَرُوا فِيهَا الْفَسادَ) الذين is either genitive as an adjective of those mentioned or accusative in censure. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The best of the views on it is that it be in the position of accusative in censure; it may be nominative, as 'they are those who transgressed', or genitive, describing those mentioned: ʿĀd, Thamūd and Pharaoh." The clause طغوا is the ṣila of الذين, and في البلاد are two [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to طغوا. (فَصَبَّ عَلَيْهِمْ رَبُّكَ سَوْطَ عَذابٍ) The فاء is a conjunction; صبّ is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; عليهم are two [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to صبّ; ربك is the agent; and سوط عذاب is a direct object. The meaning of this expression will come in the section of Rhetoric. (إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَبِالْمِرْصادِ) The clause has no position, because it is a justification for what precedes; إن and its noun; the shifted lām; and بالمرصاد are two [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to an omitted word that is the predicate of إن. Its meaning too will come in the section of Rhetoric.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «فصبّ عليهم ربك سوط عذاب» is an implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya). He used "pouring", which is particular to water, because it requires swiftness in descent upon the one struck. He said:
فصبّ عليهم محصرات كأنها ... شآبيب ليست من سحاب ولا قطر
(So He poured on them besieging [showers], as though they were downpours that were neither from cloud nor rain.)
And another said, describing horses:
صببنا عليهم ظالمين سياطنا ... فطارت بها أيد سراع وأرجل
(We poured on them, unjustly, our whips, and swift hands and legs flew with them.)
He borrowed the whip for the punishment because it requires of repetition and recurrence what the sword and others do not. The wording of al-Zamakhsharī is beautiful of its kind. He said: "One says: 'he poured the whip on him', 'covered him with it' and 'hooded him with it'. The mention of the whip is an indication that what He sent down upon them in this world of great punishment, measured against what He has prepared for them in the next, is like the whip when measured against everything else with which one is tortured." Al-sawṭ, as in the Qāmūs, is mixing, or that you mix two things in your vessel and then beat them with your hand until they mix, like al-taswīṭ; and the whip because it mixes flesh with blood; the plural is siyāṭ and aswāṭ. Al-Farrāʾ said: "It is a word the Arabs say for every kind of punishment. The origin of that is that the whip is their punishment with which they are tortured, so it came to be used for every punishment when it is at the extreme of punishment."
2- In His saying «إن ربك لبالمرصاد» is a representational metaphor (istiʿāra tamthīliyya). He likened the Exalted's being keeper of the deeds of servants, watching over them and requiting what is small and great of them, so that none escapes Him in any case, to one who sits on the road lying in wait for whoever travels it, to seize him and do to him what he wishes; then the word of one of them was applied to the other.

* Benefits:
The Qur'anic story, in its subject, its manner of presentation, its choice of events and the sequence of its scenes, submitted to the requirements of religious purposes, and the traces of this submission appeared in many features. But this complete submission to religious purposes, and its fulfilling this purpose in full, did not prevent the artistic characteristics from standing out in its presentation, especially in depiction, which is the most prominent characteristic of the Qur'an. We would have liked to transmit to you the story of Dhāt al-ʿImād as the narrators and exegetes transmitted it, but the matter would be long, so it suffices us to transmit its summary, that you may glimpse in its light its artistic characteristics, and then refer you to the longer works. They narrated that ʿĀd had two sons, Shaddād and Shadīd, who ruled and prevailed; then Shadīd died and the matter fell wholly to Shaddād, who ruled the world and whose kings submitted to him. He heard of the mention of Paradise and said: "I shall build the like of it." So he built Iram in one of the deserts of ʿAdan over three hundred years, and his age was nine hundred years. It is a great city, upon which imagination bestowed marvels of wonderful description: its palaces of gold and silver, its columns of chrysolite and ruby, and in it were all kinds of trees and flowing rivers. When its building was complete, he set out toward it with the people of his kingdom; when he was a day and a night's journey away, Allah sent upon them a cry from the sky and they perished. It is reported from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qilāba that he went out seeking camels of his, and happened upon it, and carried off what he could of what was there. His news reached Muʿāwiya, who summoned him, and he told him; he sent to Kaʿb and asked him, and he said: "It is Iram Dhāt al-ʿImād, and a man of the Muslims will enter it in your time, ruddy, fair-haired, short, with a mole on his brow and a mole on his heel, who goes out seeking camels of his." Then he turned and saw Ibn Abī Qilāba and said: "By Allah, this is that man." In any case, this has no religious basis to rely on, and various superstitions have been introduced and fabricated tales and contrived legends woven into the exegesis of the Book of Allah, glory be to Him.

dervis-irab:15-30.t:
* Vocabulary:
(التُّراثَ) Inheritance; the tāʾ is a substitute for wāw because it is from wirātha (inheriting), as they said in tujāh, tukhma and tukaʾa.
(لَمًّا) Gathering, devouring. In al-Mukhtār: "akl lammā of the thing he did, of the pattern radda; one says: 'Allah gathered (lamma) his disorder', i.e. He set right and gathered what was scattered of his affair." Abū ʿUbayda said: "lamamtu what was on the table when I ate everything on it entirely." Al-Ḥuṭayʾa said:
إذا كان لما يتبع الذّم ربه ... فلا قدّس الرحمن تلك الطواحنا
(If devouring is what disgrace follows in its owner, then may the Merciful not sanctify those grinders.)
And of it is lamamtu al-shaʿth (I gathered the disorder). Al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī said:
ولست بمستبق أخا لا تلمه ... على شعث أيّ الرجال المهذب
(You will not keep a brother whom you do not set right in his disorder; which man is refined?)
(وَثاقَهُ) In al-Miṣbāḥ: "wathuqa al-shayʾ, with ḍamma, wathāqatan: it was strong and firm, so it is wathīq, firm; awthaqtuhu: I made it firm; and al-wathāq, with fatḥa or kasra on the wāw, is the fetter, the rope and the like; the plural is wuthuq, like ribāṭ and ribuṭ."

* I'rab:
(فَأَمَّا الْإِنْسانُ إِذا مَا ابْتَلاهُ رَبُّهُ فَأَكْرَمَهُ وَنَعَّمَهُ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّي أَكْرَمَنِ) The فاء is resumptive, though the sense of al-Zamakhsharī's words is that it is a conjunction. He said: "If you say: to what is His saying 'As for man' connected? I say: to His saying «إن ربك لبالمرصاد», as though it were said: 'Allah wants from man only obedience and striving for the outcome, and He lies in wait with punishment for the disobedient; as for man, he does not want that, and is concerned only with the immediate world and what pleases and comforts him in it.'" In his words there is a clear Muʿtazilite whiff. أما is a particle of condition and elaboration; الإنسان is a mubtadaʾ; إذا is an adverbial attached to يقول; ما is redundant; the clause ابتلاه is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverbial to it; ربه is the agent; فأكرمه is conjoined to ابتلاه; ونعمه is also conjoined; the فاء is a linker because of the sense of condition in أما; and the clause يقول is the khabar of الإنسان. The adverbial's attachment to يقول, which occurs as a predicate, is not precluded, because the adverbial is intended to be postponed, the implied form being: "as for man, he is one who says 'my Lord has honored me' at the time of testing." ربي is a mubtadaʾ and the clause أكرمني is the khabar; they dropped the yāʾ from أكرمن for brevity. (وَأَمَّا إِذا مَا ابْتَلاهُ فَقَدَرَ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقَهُ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّي أَهانَنِ) Conjoined to the preceding clause, and its parsing is like its parsing. (كَلَّا بَلْ لا تُكْرِمُونَ الْيَتِيمَ وَلا تَحَاضُّونَ عَلى طَعامِ الْمِسْكِينِ) كلا is a particle of rebuke and reproach to man for his saying; بل is a particle of iḍrāb (turning away) from the ugly to the uglier, to progress in their censure; لا is negative; تكرمون اليتيم is an imperfect verb, nominative, with an agent and a direct object; ولا تحاضّون is conjoined to لا تكرمون; and على طعام المسكين are two [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to تحاضّون. (وَتَأْكُلُونَ التُّراثَ أَكْلًا لَمًّا وَتُحِبُّونَ الْمالَ حُبًّا جَمًّا) Also conjoined; التراث is the object of تأكلون; أكلا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) and لما is an adjective; and تحبون المال حبّا جمّا is also conjoined, like the preceding clause in parsing. (كَلَّا إِذا دُكَّتِ الْأَرْضُ دَكًّا دَكًّا) كلا is a particle of rebuke and reproach to them for all that; إذا is an adverbial attached to يتذكر; the clause دكّت is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverbial to it; الأرض is the deputy agent; and دكّا دكّا are two maṣdars in the position of ḥāl according to the opinion of Abū Ḥayyān and al-Zamakhsharī, the second not being emphasis; rather the repetition indicates comprehensiveness, as in "I read grammar chapter by chapter". Ibn Khālawayh parsed the first دكّا as a maṣdar and the second as emphasis, which is not remote. (وَجاءَ رَبُّكَ وَالْمَلَكُ صَفًّا صَفًّا) Conjoined to what preceded; وجاء ربك is a verb and an agent; الملك is conjoined to ربك; and صفّا صفّا is a ḥāl, i.e. "in rows" or "possessing rows". What allows the ḥāl to come as a non-derived noun is the sequence (tartīb), whose rule is that elaboration comes after mention of the whole in its two parts repeated. Al-Raḍī said: there is disagreement about the accusative of the second part: al-Zajjāj held that it is emphasis; Ibn Jinnī held that it is an adjective; al-Fārisī held that it is accusative by the first, because when it took the place of the ḥāl it could operate. Al-Murādī said: the preferred view is that it and what precedes it are accusative by the first operative, because the two together are the ḥāl, and its parallel in predicates is "this is sweet-sour". If someone held that its accusative is by conjunction with the فاء omitted in implication, the meaning being "bāban fa-bāban" and "ṣaffan fa-ṣaffan", it would be a good view. Abū l-Ḥasan stated explicitly that a conjunction particle may not enter any of the repeated items except the فاء, specifically. (وَجِيءَ يَوْمَئِذٍ بِجَهَنَّمَ يَوْمَئِذٍ يَتَذَكَّرُ الْإِنْسانُ وَأَنَّى لَهُ الذِّكْرى) The واو is a conjunction; جيء is a past passive verb; يومئذ is an adverbial annexed to its like, attached to جيء; بجهنم is in the position of nominative as deputy agent; the second يومئذ is an adverbial annexed to its like and is a badal (substitute) for إذا; the clause يتذكر الإنسان has no position because it is the response to إذا; the واو is a ḥāl-wāw; أنى is an interrogative noun whose meaning is negation, in the position of accusative as an adverbial of place, attached to an omitted fronted predicate; وله are two [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to what the adverbial is attached to; and الذكرى is a postponed mubtadaʾ. An omitted muḍāf must be implied, i.e. "and from where would he have the benefit of the reminder", otherwise there would be contradiction and inconsistency between "he remembers" and "how could he have the reminder". (يَقُولُ: يا لَيْتَنِي قَدَّمْتُ لِحَياتِي) The clause is a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) for the clause يتذكر, or a resumption that came as an answer to a question arising from it, as though it were said "What does he say upon his remembering?", and it was said "He says". يا is a particle of alert, or the one addressed is omitted; ليتني: ليت and its noun; the clause قدمت is its predicate; ولحياتي are two [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to قدمت; and the vocative clause is the content of the saying. (فَيَوْمَئِذٍ لا يُعَذِّبُ عَذابَهُ أَحَدٌ وَلا يُوثِقُ وَثاقَهُ أَحَدٌ) The فاء is a conjunction; يومئذ is an adverbial attached to يعذب, and the tanwīn is a compensation for a clause that conveys the preceding terror of the situation; لا is negative; يعذب is an active imperfect verb; عذابه is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and the pronoun in عذابه refers to Allah
. It is surprising of Ibn Khālawayh that he parsed it as a direct object, and I do not know what his viewpoint is. أحد is the agent of يعذب. It was read يعذَّب in the passive, in which case أحد is the deputy agent and the pronoun in عذابه refers to the unbeliever. The wording of al-Qurṭubī on this point: "«فيومئذ لا يعذب عذابه أحد», i.e. no one punishes like Allah's punishment, and no one binds like His binding, the pronoun referring to Allah the Exalted, and this is the saying of Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan. Al-Kisāʾī read لا يعذَّب ولا يوثَق with fatḥa on the dhāl and the thāʾ, i.e. no one is punished in this world like Allah's punishment of the unbeliever on that day, and none is bound as the unbeliever is bound." His saying ولا يوثق etc. is conjoined to the preceding clause, and what was said in parsing the first is said about it. Ibn Khālawayh cited an interesting discussion which we quote here: "'ولا يوثق' is a conjunction upon يعذب; the maṣdar is awthaqa, yūthiqu, īthāqan, so he is mūthaq. If someone says: is it permissible to pronounce yūthiq with hamza as yuʾmin is pronounced with hamza? Say: that is not permissible, because in awthaqa the fāʾ of the verb [first radical] is like awfaḍa, yūfiḍu, asraʿa, yusriʿu, awrā, yūrī, and awqada, yūqidu, all of which are without hamza. Allah, mighty and majestic, said: «إلى نصب يوفضون» and «النار التي تورون». The hamza is pronounced only in those whose first radical is a hamza, such as āmana, yuʾminu, because the original is aʾmana, and they found two hamzas at the beginning of a word heavy, so the second was softened; so know that. If the first radical is a yāʾ, like aysara, ayqana and ayfaʿa al-ghulām, the yāʾ is turned into wāw in the imperfect because of the ḍamma before it and its quiescence, and it is also not permissible to pronounce it with hamza, as in yūqinūna, yūfiʿu al-ghulām and yūsiru. Abū l-Ḥasan the reciter told me: Abū Khalīfa al-Baṣrī narrated from al-Māzinī from al-Akhfash, who said: I heard Abū Ḥayya al-Numayrī say 'yuʾqinūn' with hamza; and Abū Ḥayya is the one who says:
إذا مضغت بعد امتناع من الضحى ... أنابيب من عود الأراك المخلّق
سقت شعب المسواك ماء غمامة ... فضيضا بجادي العراق المروّق
(When, after the height of forenoon has passed, she chews pieces of perfumed arāk wood, the toothstick's strands are watered with cloud-water, flowing, scented with saffron of Iraq, clarified.)
However, some of the Arabs pronounce with hamza what is not pronounced with hamza, likening it to what is, as in their saying 'ḥalaʾtu al-sawīq' and 'rathaʾtu al-mayyit'. Aḥmad told me from ʿAlī from Abū ʿUbayda, who said: al-Ḥasan read «ولا أدرأكم به» with hamza, and it is a mistake according to the grammarians, because it is from darayt." (يا أَيَّتُهَا النَّفْسُ الْمُطْمَئِنَّةُ، ارْجِعِي إِلى رَبِّكِ راضِيَةً مَرْضِيَّةً) The clause is in the position of accusative by an omitted "saying", i.e. "Allah says to the believer". يا is a particle of vocative; أية is an indefinite specified one addressed, indeclinable on the ḍamma, and parallels have occurred often; the هاء is for alert; النفس is a badal (substitute); المطمئنة is an adjective of النفس; ارجعي is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the yāʾ is the agent; وإلى ربك are two [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to ارجعي; and راضية مرضية are two ḥāls. (فَادْخُلِي فِي عِبادِي وَادْخُلِي جَنَّتِي) In sequence upon ارجعي; وفي عبادي are two [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to ادخلي; and وادخلي جنتي is also conjoined, i.e. "enter into their ranks and enter My Paradise with them."

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «وجاء ربك والملك صفّا صفّا» is the art of excess in description (ifrāṭ fī l-ṣifa), as Ibn al-Muʿtazz named it; Qudāma named it mubālagha (hyperbole), others named it tablīgh, and Qudāma's naming is the well-known one. He defined it by saying: it is that the speaker mentions a state which, were he to stop at it, would suffice, but he does not stop at it until he adds in his speech what is more eloquent in the meaning he intends. It has various kinds, among them putting the speech in the form of reporting of the greatest, mightiest, for hyperbole, while the report about him is figurative, as the saying of someone who sees a great procession or a vast army, "The king himself has come", while knowing that what has come is his army. In the verse He made the coming of the mightiest of His signs a coming of Himself, glory be to Him.

* Benefits:
1- أيها and أيتها: the majority read «يا أيتها النفس» with the feminine tāʾ, and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read يا أيها without tāʾ. We know of no one who mentioned that it may be masculine even when the one addressed is feminine except the author of al-Badīʿ, and this verse is witness to that. There is an analogical reason for it: since it is not dualized or pluralized in addressing duals and plurals, so it is not made masculine in addressing the feminine either. أي and أية are indeclinable on the ḍamma because each is a single one addressed, and the alerting hāʾ in them is redundant and inseparable from the word, i.e. and أية as a compensation for the muḍāf ilayhi, with fatḥa on the hāʾ.
2- How dakhala is made transitive: when what is entered is not a true container (ẓarf), dakhala is made transitive to it by في, as in "I entered into the matter" and "I entered into the throng of people", and of it is «فادخلي في عبادي», i.e. among My righteous servants; and when what is entered is a true container, it is generally transitive to it without the mediation of في, and of it is «وادخلي جنتي». In any case جنتي is parsed as a direct object by extension, because in origin it is not transitive by itself, as has preceded.
